To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of students on a test of financial awareness is positively and significantly affected by: the length of time since the student first studied accountancy, the number of years of study at university, the student’s age, and the student’s gender (female students tend to perform better).
In summary, our research is concerned with

1. the extent to which the level of students’ financial awareness is affected by their age; 2. the impact of students’ gender and educational background; 3. the effect of pre-university experience of accountancy; 4. the impact of work experience; 5. the influence of students’ investment holding; 6. the effect of university courses in accountants and related subjects; and 7. the impact of the students’ overall performance.

the extent to which the performance of university students in an examination of basic accounting and finance knowledge varies with age, gender, education background, work experience, investment holdings and exposure to university courses; and whether the results of such a study can be generalised across different subject disciplines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of the first group of students, financial awareness is not significantly related to any of the variables examined.
the determinants of students’ financial awareness are complex and varied, and that the results are not always consistent.
the determinants of financial awareness are not as straightforward as might have been thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the more students are exposed to accountancy and related subjects the better they do in the test.
students' financial awareness is significantly related to their age, gender and the level of accountancy tuition they have received.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance in the financial awareness test is significantly related to the amount of accountancy tuition received by students.

the performance of first-year students in the financial awareness test is significantly related to their pre-university exposure to accountancy and related subjects, but not to the number of years of formal university-level study in accountancy.
the level of financial awareness is positively related to a student’s age.
